```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# import files:
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

electricity_generation_by_source <- read_csv("electricity-generation-by-source.csv")
economic_damage_from_natural_disasters_wind <- read_csv("economic-damage-from-natural-disasters.csv")
```

## Data cleanup

here we clean up the electrricity generation data:

```{r plot-data}
# import files:
# View(electricity_generation_by_source |> filter(Entity == "World"))
plotdata <- 
  electricity_generation_by_source |> 
  filter(Entity == "World") |>
  full_join(economic_damage_from_natural_disasters |> filter(Entity == "Extreme weather"), join_by(Year))
  
  #View()
```


```{r plot-test 1}

# 2. Create the scatter plot
plot(plotdata$Year, plotdata$Wind,
     xlab = "Year", ylab = "Energy generated by source. wind")
```

```{r plot-test2}
# 2. Find a scaling factor based on your data maximums
# Example: If Max Damages = 1,000,000 and Max Energy = 1,000, the factor is 1,000
max_energy <- max(plotdata$Wind, na.rm = TRUE)
max_damages <- max(plotdata$`Total economic damages`, na.rm = TRUE)
scale_factor <- max_damages / max_energy

# Plot manually layered lines
ggplot(plotdata, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Wind, color = "Wind Energy"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = `Total economic damages` / scale_factor, color = "Damages (USD)"), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Configure the Y-Axes
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Wind Energy",
    labels = scales::comma,
    # Re-multiply by the factor to display the correct numbers on the right side
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * scale_factor, name = "Damages (USD)", labels = scales::dollar)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Wind Energy" = "blue", "Damages (USD)" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Wind Energy and Damages Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Value",
    color = "Legend"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
